answer: To stop Sybil attacks, identity creation requires anchoring each vertex to a verifiable deposit bond. Every new node must submit proof of locked capital, turning each registered identity into a costly relic that is slashed upon coordinated misbehavior. Furthermore, the protocol inspects peer topology like a barrier reef, isolating untrusted clusters and denying them consensus weight. An attacker attempting to deploy a swarm of fraudulent agents faces superlinear capital lockup costs and immediate slashing across all coordinated nodes.
